#1 I am stuck with understanding the rational cohomology of the group-completed configuration space of points in Euclidean 3-space

ΩB⊔Conf(R3) \Omega B_{{}_{\sqcup}} \mathrm{Conf}\big( \mathbb{R}^3 \big) ΩB⊔​​Conf(R3)

where Conf(R3)\mathrm{Conf}\big( \mathbb{R}^3 \big)Conf(R3) is a topological monoid under disjoint union of configurations of points (after translating them a little; as on p. 1-2 of Segal 73).

I know the rational cohomology abstractly, but I am stuck interpreting the generators:

Namely, by Theorem 1 in Segal 73 and by Example 2.5 in Møller-Raussen 85 we have a rational equivalence

ΩB⊔Conf(R3)⟶Segal73≃Ω3S3⟶Moller−Raussen85≃Q⊔n≠0∈NS3 \Omega B_{{}_{\sqcup}} \mathrm{Conf}\big( \mathbb{R}^3 \big) \underset{\simeq}{\overset{\mathrm{Segal} 73}{\longrightarrow}} \Omega^3 S^3 \underset{\simeq_{\mathbb{Q}}}{\overset{\mathrm{Moller}-\mathrm{Raussen} 85}{\longrightarrow}} \underset{ n \neq 0 \in \mathbb{N} }{\sqcup} S^3 ΩB⊔​​Conf(R3)≃⟶Segal73​​Ω3S3≃Q​⟶Moller−Raussen85​​n=0∈N⊔​S3

So the rational cohomology of each connected component of ΩB⊔Conf(R3)\Omega B_{{}_{\sqcup}} \mathrm{Conf}\big( \mathbb{R}^3 \big)ΩB⊔​​Conf(R3) is free on a degree 3 generator, except in the connected component of the base point, where it is trivial.

I am stuck understanding what these degree-3 generators are in terms of configurations of (virtual) points.

One idea was to use the group completion theorem to express

H∙(ΩB⊔Conf(R3),Q)≃??H∙(Conf(R3),Q)[(π0)−1] H_\bullet \big( \Omega B_{{}_{\sqcup}} \mathrm{Conf}\big( \mathbb{R}^3 \big), \mathbb{Q} \big) \overset{??}{\simeq} H_\bullet \big( \mathrm{Conf} \big( \mathbb{R}^3 \big), \mathbb{Q} \big) \big[ (\pi_0)^{-1} \big] H∙​(ΩB⊔​​Conf(R3),Q)≃??H∙​(Conf(R3),Q)[(π0​)−1]

I am unsure if the assumption of the group completion theorem is met (that π0\pi_0π0​ is in the center of the Pontrjagin ring). It seems intuitively obvious, but there might be a pitfall. The author of the first lines of arXiv:math/0511645 thinks that it applies.

But assuming the group completion theorem applies, I next run into a contradiction, since

H∙(Confn(R3),Q)  =  Q H_\bullet \big( \mathrm{Conf}_n\big( \mathbb{R}^3 \big), \mathbb{Q} \big) \;=\; \mathbb{Q} H∙​(Confn​(R3),Q)=Q

is just trivial. (One quick argument is that it’s the Sym(n)\mathrm{Sym}(n)Sym(n)-invariants in this space, which are trivial. It’s also a special case of Theorem 4 in arXiv:math/0311323.)

So I guess this means that the assumptions of the McDuff-Segal group completion theorem are not actually met here for the ⊔\sqcup⊔-monoid of configurations in R3\mathbb{R}^3R3. (??)

Or else I am making some silly mistake elsewhere.
subject: cohomology of group-completed configuration space?

#9 I was wrong in #6: That fact you pointed to in #5 (here) is what I need:

The scanning map

Confn(Rk)⟶ΩkSk∣deg=n \mathrm{Conf}_n\big( \mathbb{R}^k \big) \longrightarrow \Omega^k S^k {}_{\vert {\mathrm{deg}} = n}Confn​(Rk)⟶ΩkSk∣deg=n​

induces an isomorphism in cohomoloigy in degrees ≤n/2\leq n/2≤n/2.

(I was previously conflating nnn with kkk, since I have this urge to confuse myself by sticking to a different convention than everyone else uses…)

Where is this actually proven?

On the first page of Segal 73 this is attributed to Barratt-Priddy 72 and Quillen 94.

But I haven’t yet spotted it in either (of the second I only have a GoogleBooks-copy, which only shows the first few pages)

#11 So I finally understood my silly mistake that led to the above confusion.

The correct rational model of Ω3S3\Omega^3 S^3Ω3S3 is instead ≃Q⊔n∈N∗ \simeq_{\mathbb{Q}} \underset{n \in \mathbb{N}} {\sqcup} \ast≃Q​n∈N⊔​∗ (here)

and so that matches the rational cohomology of the unordered configuration space Conf(R3)\mathrm{Conf}(\mathbb{R}^3)Conf(R3) being trivial in positive degree.

My only remaining confusion is that I keep seeing a non-trivial rational 2-cocycle on the loop space ΩConfn(R3)\Omega {\mathrm{Conf}}_n(\mathbb{R}^3)ΩConfn​(R3) of the unordered configuration space for n≥3n \geq 3n≥3 points:

Namely the Sym-invariant part of the respective graph complex is a dg-model for Confn(R3)\mathrm{Conf}_n(\mathbb{R}^3)Confn​(R3) itself, and so its based loop space is modeled by shifting all graphs down in degree by 1, and keeping only the co-unary part of the differential.

But the 3-point interaction vertex has co-binary differential, exhibiting the “3-term relation”. Hence after passing to based loops, this becomes a closed 2-cocycle.

Moreover, it seems immediate that this 2-cocycle is not exact: The only possible form of a trivialization is the graph obtained from it by inserting a single internal edge in the essentially unique way, and a quick explicit check shows that the differential of that is not the 3-point interaction vertex (but is zero).

But if this is the case, we found a non-trivial 2 class on ΩConf3(R3)\Omega {\mathrm{Conf}}_3(\mathbb{R}^3)ΩConf3​(R3); and then by adding in more disconnected free vertices also on all ΩConfn≥3(R3)\Omega {\mathrm{Conf}}_{n \geq 3}(\mathbb{R}^3)ΩConfn≥3​(R3).

At the same time, all these are loop spaces of rationally contractible spaces by the above.

That’s a contradiction.

I see two possibilities: Either I am making a really basic mistake in unwinding the definition of the graph differential. Or I am unwittingly violating some simply-connectedness assumption that invalidates the model for the looped configuration space by degree-shifted graphs.

Hm…
